name: The Thing I Quit
why_it_works: Quitting something is more believable than adding something. When an owner admits they stopped a common industry habit, the viewer reads it as a values choice with a cost, and a cost is proof the owner means it. It also quietly signals that competitors still do the old thing.

hook.pattern: Open on the confession: name the specific habit you stopped, then hint it cost you money.
examples: Most shops never stop {{old_habit}}. We did.

variables.name: trade
variables.description: What kind of business this is, in plain words, 2 words or fewer

variables.name: old_habit
variables.description: The common industry habit the owner quit, lowercase, 3 words or fewer

variables.name: cost_of_quitting
variables.description: What quitting cost them at first, lowercase, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: we turned away about ten walk-ins a week

variables.name: what_changed
variables.description: The concrete result after quitting, lowercase, 12 words or fewer
variables.example: nobody waits past their slot, and regulars rebook before they leave

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer can do now, starting with a capital-letter verb, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: Book a slot that starts on time

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Fine-print disclosure line for the client's regulated niche (use the matching compliance pack's disclosure line)
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 portrait of the owner of {{brand}} leaning on the counter of their {{trade}}, arms crossed, direct eye contact, late afternoon window light, slightly serious expression, shallow depth of field

beats.voiceover: Every {{trade}} does it. It looks like more money.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of an empty chair or station inside {{brand}}, a clock visible on the wall, cool muted light, quiet mood, no people
Vertical 9:16 slow push-in on a relaxed customer mid-service at {{brand}}, warm practical lighting, calm unhurried motion, candid feel

beats.on_screen_text: Less, done right, beats more, done fast.
beats.voiceover: Less, done right, beats more, done fast.

craft.notes: The cost beat is what makes the claim believable, so never skip it or soften it into a humblebrag. Say one real number if you have one. Keep the result beat visual: show the calm, don't describe it.

do_not: Pick a habit nobody actually does, or the confession has no stakes
Insult other shops that still do it; the contrast is implied
Claim a result you cannot show on camera or back with a number
compliance: Fitness trainers: no weight, body or health result claims; if a result is shown, state typical results
Coaches: no income, revenue or 'quit your job' promises; any result shown is labelled not typical
The cost and result numbers must be real figures from the business, not estimates dressed as facts
